gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Trio 3 Pro's 'single USB-C cable' setup is its driver mode: it needs Mobile Pixels' software plus a power adapter plugged into the Trio, and that adapter is also what unlocks the full 300-nit rating. Without the driver it needs two DisplayPort-enabled USB-C ports, one cable per screen, which a base M1, M2 or M3 MacBook Air with its lid open cannot supply (Apple: one external display with the lid open).
standout_why: Compared against the three pages ChatGPT cited. itechguides.com '15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026' lists the Trio 3.0 Pro's connection only as 'Product-specific USB-C/video'. Its only driver point is general: 'DisplayLink is not equivalent to native DisplayPort Alt Mode'. Macworld's 'Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026' has part of the finding: it says plain M1/M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo need 'free software (rather like DisplayLink)' and lists 'Requires software installation' as a con. It does not say that one cable for both screens means driver mode, that the driver mode needs a power adapter on the Trio, or that the 300-nit rating needs that adapter. It also does not cover the base M3 Air. The RTINGS portable-monitor page body did not load in my fetch, so I could not check it. ChatGPT's own answer repeated 'single USB-C connection' for the Trio 3 Pro and the Aura Dual Boost with no driver caveat.
decides: This keeps the Trio 3 Pro as the pick for two added screens on a laptop with two video-capable USB-C ports (MacBook Pro Pro/Max, many Windows laptops), using two cables and no driver. It weakens the pick for a base M1/M2/M3 MacBook Air with its lid open, or for anyone who wants one cable: they will run Mobile Pixels' software and carry a power adapter for the Trio. The table should normalise every row on three axes: video path (native Alt Mode vs driver), cables per added screen, and whether the stated nits hold on laptop bus power. The footnote is that a 'single cable' claim on a two-screen extender means the driver path unless the maker says otherwise.
